name: git
summary: Version control in local repositories: init, add, commit, log, diff, branch, merge, stash (no network)
help: usage: git [-C <path>] [-c <name>=<value>] [--version] [--help] <command> [<args>]
Version control for the files in this machine. Repositories are ordinary .git
directories in the format real git uses, so they can be copied out and used
elsewhere, and repositories copied in (packed by git clone or git gc) can be
read and extended. There is no network: clone, fetch, pull and push are not
available, and git here writes no packs (gc, repack).
Start and save work:
init       create a repository
add        stage changes; rm, mv remove and rename tracked files
commit     record the staged changes
status     show what changed
diff       show changes as patches or statistics
restore    put back files from the index or a commit
reset      move the branch or unstage files
stash      set changes aside
clean      delete untracked files
History and branches:
log, show  look at commits
branch     list, create, rename, delete branches
switch     change branch (checkout also restores files)
merge      join histories (fast-forward or three-way with conflict markers)
tag        name a commit
bisect     find the commit that introduced a change
merge-base find a common ancestor
Patches:
apply        apply a diff to the work tree or the index
format-patch write commits as mail patches; am applies them as commits
Plumbing: rev-parse, rev-list, ls-files, cat-file, config, fsck.
'git help <command>' or 'git <command> --help' describes one command.

bisect.summary: Find the commit that introduced a change by binary search
bisect.notes: bisect run runs the command at each step: exit 0 marks the commit good, 125 skips it, 1 to 127 mark it bad, anything else stops the search. A step picks the commit that splits the remaining ones most evenly; with skipped commits the next best is taken, which may differ from real git's choice.

messages.needStart: You need to start by "git bisect start"
messages.statusBoth: status: waiting for both good and bad commits
messages.statusGood: status: waiting for good commit(s), bad commit known
messages.statusBad: status: waiting for bad commit, {count} good commit known
messages.statusBadMany: status: waiting for bad commit, {count} good commits known
messages.bisecting: Bisecting: {revisions} left to test after this (roughly {steps})
messages.runFailed: error: bisect run failed: exit code {code} from {command} is < 0 or >= 128
messages.runCannotContinue: error: bisect run cannot continue any more
messages.onlySkipped:
There are only 'skip'ped commits left to test.
The first bad commit could be any of:
{commits}
We cannot bisect more!
messages.notAvailable: error: 'git bisect {action}' is not available in this machine's git; use start, good, bad, skip, reset, log or run

gc.summary: Pack and clean up the repository (not available; packs written by real git can be read)

repack.summary: Pack loose objects (not available; packs written by real git can be read)

fsck.summary: Check the object database: every object readable, everything reachable present

options.description: list unreachable objects nothing else points to (the default; --no-dangling turns it off)
accepted and ignored (loose and packed objects are always checked)
accepted and ignored (objects are always read in full)

fsck.notes: Exit status: 0 when everything is fine (dangling objects included), otherwise 1 for an unreadable object and 2 for a missing one that something reachable needs, combined.

format-patch.summary: Write commits as mailbox patches that git am can apply

options.description: write the files into <dir> instead of the current directory
print all the patches as one mailbox instead of writing files
only the <n> newest commits (also -<n>; -1 alone means the last commit)

format-patch.notes: Each commit becomes NNNN-subject.patch: the From line, author, date, [PATCH n/m] subject, message, diffstat and patch. Merge commits are left out. Non-ASCII headers are written as UTF-8, not RFC 2047 encoded.

archive.summary: Export a tree as an archive (not available)

symbolic-ref.summary: Read or change a symbolic ref (not available)

write-tree.summary: Write the index as a tree (not available)

name-rev.summary: Name a commit after a ref (not available)

whatchanged.summary: Show the log with changes (not available)

notes: Implemented from the published repository format and observed behaviour of git 2.43 (Ubuntu 24.04); every text here is our own except the messages git prints. Unsupported subcommands are listed so they get a clear answer instead of 'not a git command'.
